1	# Structural BPMN (what the registry does not emit)
2	
3	The registry's `xmlTemplate`s give you the `uipath:*` payload for each node
4	(see [registry-workflow.md](registry-workflow.md)). They do **not** give you the
5	structural BPMN that holds those nodes together. This file is the ground truth
6	for everything you author by hand around the templates.
7	
8	Two sources define the contract:
9	
10	- the registry spec `bpmn-spec.json` — enumerates which BPMN element types and
11	  event definitions exist, via its `bpmnElements` section;
12	- the Studio Web canvas serializer
13	  (`PO.Frontend/src/services/serialization/`) — defines how that XML must be
14	  shaped to import and round-trip.
15	
16	Where the registry stops, the canvas serializer is authoritative. Each
17	gap below is labelled **REGISTRY GAP** — the registry exposes no template for
18	it, so author it from this reference.
19	
20	BPMN XML element names are case-sensitive. Use the exact lower-camel BPMN tag
21	names the serializer emits, such as `<bpmn:startEvent>`,
22	`<bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>`, `<bpmn:scriptTask>`, and `<bpmn:endEvent>`.
23	Do not use PascalCase variants like `<bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent>`; XML accepts
24	them syntactically, but BPMN tools do not treat them as the same elements.
25	
26	## The document scaffold (REGISTRY GAP)
27	
28	The registry emits no `<bpmn:definitions>` / `<bpmn:process>` root and no
29	namespace declarations. Author this shell yourself. The canvas import detector
30	(`exporter.ts`) requires: a root `<…:definitions>` carrying a BPMN-spec
31	namespace, at least one `<bpmn:process>`, and (to render) a
32	`<bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>`.
33	
34	```xml
35	<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
36	<bpmn:definitions
37	    xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL"
38	    xmlns:bpmndi="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/DI"
39	    xmlns:dc="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DC"
40	    xmlns:di="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DI"
41	    xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
42	    xmlns:uipath="http://uipath.org/schema/bpmn"
43	    id="Definitions_1" targetNamespace="http://bpmn.io/schema/bpmn"
44	    exporter="UiPath (https://bpmn.uipath.com)" exporterVersion="1.0">
45	  <bpmn:process id="Process_1" isExecutable="true">
46	    <!-- variables, flow nodes, sequence flows -->
47	  </bpmn:process>
48	  <bpmndi:BPMNDiagram id="Diagram_1">
49	    <bpmndi:BPMNPlane id="Plane_1" bpmnElement="Process_1">
50	      <!-- one BPMNShape per node, one BPMNEdge per flow -->
51	    </bpmndi:BPMNPlane>
52	  </bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>
53	</bpmn:definitions>
54	```
55	
56	The `uipath:` namespace URI is exactly `http://uipath.org/schema/bpmn`. All
57	`uipath:*` tags inside `extensionElements` are lower-camelCase
58	(`uipath:activity`, `uipath:variables`, `uipath:loopCharacteristics`, …).
59	
60	Every `uipath:activity` / `uipath:event` / `uipath:mapping` carries its node
61	type as a **child** element — `<uipath:type value="<Type>" version="v1" />` —
62	never as a `type=` attribute on the wrapper. This holds both for templated nodes
63	and for any shell you author or preserve by hand.
64	
65	XML comments must not contain `--` (double-hyphen): it is invalid XML and the
66	file will fail to parse. Never paste CLI commands or flags
67	(`--output`, `--connection-id`) into `<!-- … -->`. Keep comments minimal.
68

138	
139	## Variables (`BPMN.Variables`)
140	
141	Declare root variables with the `BPMN.Variables` registry template attached to
142	the process via `extensionElements`, or use the canvas `<uipath:variables>`
143	block directly. Variable bodies are CDATA. Reference variables in expressions as
144	`vars.<id>` — see [expression-authoring.md](expression-authoring.md).
145	Sub-process-scoped variables go in that sub-process's own `<uipath:variables>`.
146	For a value produced only by a task output, prefer root
147	`<uipath:output id="..." name="..." type="..." />`; preserve the exact id and
148	target that same id from `uipath:output var="..."`.
149	
150	## Script tasks (`BPMN.ScriptTask`) — Jint runtime contract
151	
152	`bpmn:scriptTask scriptFormat="JavaScript"` runs under **Jint**, not Node.js or
153	a browser. The mapping payload comes from the `BPMN.ScriptTask` registry
154	template, but the runtime contract is fixed:
155	
156	- Only these helpers exist: `uipath.aggregate`, `uipath._aggregate`,
157	  `uipath._pipe`, and a no-op `console`. No npm packages, filesystem, network,
158	  browser globals, or long-running async behavior. Execution envelope is ~64 MB
159	  / 30 s.
160	- Set `uipath:scriptVersion value="v3"` for new scripts; preserve an imported
161	  `value="v2"`. For v2+ the script returns JSON under `response`.
162	- Mapped `args` fields are read as **top-level identifiers** in the script body
163	  (`amount`, not `args.amount`); the input mapping itself stays `name="args"`
164	  with `type="json"` and `target="bodyField"`, and maps each field by variable
165	  id (`=vars.Var_Amount`). Include `<uipath:input name="args" type="json"
166	  target="bodyField"><![CDATA[{}]]></uipath:input>` even when there are no
167	  inputs; this is part of the `BPMN.ScriptTask` registry template.
168	- Map the returned object's property back through `source="=result.response"`
169	  (the conventional scalar property) or `source="=result.response.<field>"`
170	  (another object field); `var` points at a declared variable id (do not put the
171	  target id in `name`).
172	- When the output mapping uses `source="=result.response"`, return an object
173	  with a `response` property, such as `return { response: 6 * 7 };`. Do not
174	  return the bare primitive `42` for that mapping shape; there is no
175	  `response` property to bind, so the runtime variable stays empty.
176	- Do not use `source="=result"` with a bare scalar return in live debug/runtime
177	  BPMN. Studio Web can report `FinalStatus: Completed` while the target root
178	  variable still reads back as `{}` or `null` from
179	  `debug-instance variables-all`.
180	- For live debug/runtime runs, never use `source="=this.result"` or
181	  `<uipath:type value="BPMN.Variables" ...>` on a script task output mapping.
182	  That older structural-test shape can pass local validation but leaves root
183	  variables `null` or faults in Studio Web. Use the `BPMN.ScriptTask` mapping
184	  with `source="=result.response"`.
185	- Do not mutate `Globals.*`, `vars.*`, or process variables inside the script
186	  body. The supported path is: return a value from the script, then use a
187	  `uipath:output` mapping to write it to the declared variable. Direct mutation
188	  is not applied to the runtime, so the variable reads empty afterward.
189	
190	```xml
191	<bpmn:scriptTask id="Task_RiskScore" name="Risk Score" scriptFormat="JavaScript">
192	  <bpmn:extensionElements>
193	    <uipath:scriptVersion value="v3" />
194	    <uipath:mapping version="v1">
195	      <uipath:type value="BPMN.ScriptTask" version="v1" />
196	      <uipath:input name="args" type="json" target="bodyField"><![CDATA[{"amount":"=vars.Var_Amount","daysOverdue":"=vars.Var_DaysOverdue"}]]></uipath:input>
197	      <uipath:output name="riskScore" type="number" var="Var_RiskScore" source="=result.response" />
198	    </uipath:mapping>
199	  </bpmn:extensionElements>
200	  <bpmn:script><![CDATA[
201	var score = amount * 0.01 + daysOverdue * 2;
202	return { response: score };
203	]]></bpmn:script>
204	</bpmn:scriptTask>
205	```
206	
207	## Sequence flows, conditions, and gateway defaults (REGISTRY GAP)
208	
209	The registry never emits `<bpmn:sequenceFlow>`, conditions, or the gateway
210	`default` attribute. Author all of them.
211	
212	- A flow: `<bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_1" sourceRef="A" targetRef="B" />`. The
213	  source/target nodes must also list `<bpmn:incoming>`/`<bpmn:outgoing>`
214	  (the registry templates leave `{incomingEdge}`/`{outgoingEdge}` placeholders
215	  for exactly these).
216	- Conditional flow body: `<bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">=vars.Var_X == "approved"</bpmn:conditionExpression>`.
217	  The canvas normalizes the body to start with `=` — always lead with `=`.
218	- Gateway default flow: set `default="Flow_else"` on the gateway element, and
219	  give that flow no condition.
220	
221	## Gateways
222	
223	Author these gateway types for new BPMN: `bpmn:ExclusiveGateway`,
224	`bpmn:ParallelGateway`, `bpmn:InclusiveGateway`, `bpmn:EventBasedGateway`.
225	`bpmn:ComplexGateway` round-trips structurally but is **preserve-only** — do not
226	generate it for new authoring (see [Do not generate for new
227	authoring](#do-not-generate-for-new-authoring-preserve-on-round-trip-only)).
228	
229	- **Exclusive (XOR)**: each non-default outgoing flow needs a
230	  `conditionExpression`; exactly one outgoing flow is the `default`. (Validator
231	  rule `MISSING_CONDITION_EXPRESSION`.)
232	- **Parallel (AND)**: fork = one in, many out; join = many in, one out. No
233	  conditions.
234	- **Inclusive (OR)**: conditions on outgoing flows; multiple may be taken.
235	- **Event-based**: routes to the first of several catch events / receive tasks
236	  to fire; its outgoing flows target intermediate catch events or receive tasks.
237	- A gateway with exactly one incoming and one outgoing flow is rejected
238	  (`SUPERFLUOUS_GATEWAY`). Activities/events must not have more than one
239	  incoming flow — join with a gateway, not a "fake join" (`FAKE_JOIN`).
240	
241	## Events and the event-definition matrix
242	
243	`bpmn-spec.json` `bpmnElements.events` enumerates which event definitions each
244	event element can carry on **round-trip**. For **new authoring**, only the
245	**none**, **Message**, **Timer**, **Error** (on end + boundary), and
246	**Terminate** (on end events only) definitions are generated. Conditional,
247	Signal, Escalation, Compensate, Cancel, Link, multiple, and parallel-multiple
248	definitions are **preserve-only** — keep them when imported, but do not generate
249	them for new BPMN (see [Do not generate for new
250	authoring](#do-not-generate-for-new-authoring-preserve-on-round-trip-only)).
251	
252	The matrix below is the round-trip acceptance per element; **preserve-only**
253	marks definitions that the skill keeps but does not author for new files.
254	
255	| Event element | Authorable | Preserve-only (round-trip) |
256	| --- | --- | --- |
257	| `bpmn:StartEvent` | none, Message, Timer | Conditional, Signal |
258	| `bpmn:IntermediateThrowEvent` | none, Message | Escalation, Signal, Link, Compensate |
259	| `bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent` | Message, Timer | Escalation, Signal, Conditional, Link, Compensate |
260	| `bpmn:EndEvent` | none, Message, Error, Terminate | Escalation, Compensate, Signal |
261	| `bpmn:BoundaryEvent` | Message, Timer, Error | Escalation, Conditional, Signal, Compensate |
262	
263	Payload shapes the canvas serializes:
264	
265	- **Timer**: `<bpmn:timerEventDefinition><bpmn:timeDuration xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">PT30M</bpmn:timeDuration></bpmn:timerEventDefinition>`
266	  (or `timeDate` / `timeCycle`). Static durations must be valid ISO-8601;
267	  week designators (`PnW`) are unsupported. Expression-mode is allowed and
268	  accepts either prefix — `=…` or `@…`.
269	- **Message**: `<bpmn:messageEventDefinition messageRef="Message_1" />` with a
270	  `<bpmn:message id="Message_1" name="…"/>` declared at definitions level. The
271	  Maestro internal-message events (`Maestro.ReceiveMessageEvent` /
272	  `Maestro.SendMessageEvent`) carry the `uipath:event` payload **and** a bare
273	  `<bpmn:messageEventDefinition />` (see their registry templates).
274	  A mid-flow wait for an inbound message is a
275	  `<bpmn:intermediateCatchEvent>` with incoming and outgoing sequence flows,
276	  the registry-provided `Maestro.ReceiveMessageEvent` payload under
277	  `bpmn:extensionElements`, and a sibling `<bpmn:messageEventDefinition />`.
278	  Do not model a mid-flow receive as `bpmn:receiveTask`, `bpmn:serviceTask`, a
279	  start event, or the PascalCase `bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent`.
280	- **Error**: `<bpmn:errorEventDefinition errorRef="Error_1" />` with a
281	  `<bpmn:error id="Error_1" name="…" errorCode="…"/>` at definitions level. An
282	  error end event with no `errorRef` fails to parse at runtime
283	  (`ERROR_END_EVENT_MISSING_EXCEPTION`); an error referenced by a boundary event
284	  must declare an `errorCode` (`ERROR_BOUNDARY_EVENT_REQUIRES_ERROR_CODE`).
285	- **Terminate** (end events only): emit the bare
286	  `<bpmn:terminateEventDefinition />`.
287	
288	Preserve-only payloads — keep these when imported, but do not author them for
289	new files:
290	
291	- **Signal**: `<bpmn:signalEventDefinition signalRef="Signal_1" />` with a
292	  definitions-level `<bpmn:signal/>`.
293	- **Escalation**: `<bpmn:escalationEventDefinition escalationRef="Escalation_1" />`
294	  with a `<bpmn:escalation id="Escalation_1" name="…" escalationCode="…"/>`
295	  declared at definitions level (parallel to message/error/signal).
296	- **Conditional / Link / Compensate**: the bare definition element; the canvas
297	  round-trips it.
298	
299	### Boundary events (REGISTRY GAP for `attachedToRef` / `cancelActivity`)
300	
301	A boundary event attaches to an activity and catches an event on it. The
302	registry exposes no boundary template; author it:
303	
304	```xml
305	<bpmn:boundaryEvent id="Boundary_Timeout" attachedToRef="Task_DoWork" cancelActivity="true">
306	  <bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
307	    <bpmn:timeDuration xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">PT15M</bpmn:timeDuration>
308	  </bpmn:timerEventDefinition>
309	  <bpmn:outgoing>Flow_OnTimeout</bpmn:outgoing>
310	</bpmn:boundaryEvent>
311	```
312	
313	- `attachedToRef` = id of the activity it sits on. The boundary event and that
314	  activity must be `flowElements` of the same parent scope.
315	- `cancelActivity="true"` = interrupting (default); `cancelActivity="false"` =
316	  non-interrupting. Per the spec, non-interrupting is available for
317	  Message/Timer/Escalation/Conditional/Signal — **not** Error or Compensate.
318	- Only one catch-all (no `errorRef`) error boundary event per task, and no two
319	  error boundary events with the same error code on one task
320	  (`MULTIPLE_CATCH_ALL_BOUNDARY_EVENTS_ON_TASK`,
321	  `DUPLICATE_ERROR_BOUNDARY_EVENT_ON_TASK`).
322	
323	### Retry and error mapping (REGISTRY GAP)
324	
325	UiPath-specific retry and error-mapping metadata live inside an activity's
326	`extensionElements`. The error **code** lives on the declared
327	`bpmn:error errorCode="…"`; `uipath:*` elements reference it through `errorRef`.
328	
329	```xml
330	<uipath:retry maxRetryCount="2" retryBackoff="PT30S" retryBackoffType="exponential"
331	              maxDuration="PT5M" exponentialBase="2" retryAllErrors="false">
332	  <uipath:errorDefinition errorRef="Error_ServiceUnavailable" />
333	</uipath:retry>
334	<uipath:errorMapping version="v1">
335	  <uipath:error id="Mapped_ServiceUnavailable" errorRef="Error_ServiceUnavailable"
336	                priority="1" condition="=vars.error.code == "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE""
337	                detail="Service unavailable" retryable="true" />
338	</uipath:errorMapping>
339	```
340	
341	- `uipath:retry` attributes: `maxRetryCount`, `retryBackoff`, `retryBackoffType`,
342	  `maxDuration`, `exponentialBase`, `retryAllErrors`. Do not use stale aliases
343	  (`maxAttempts`, `interval`).
344	- `uipath:error` (mapping) fields: `id`, `errorRef`, `priority`, `condition`,
345	  `detail`, `retryable` (`true`/`false`). Conditions read the runtime error via
346	  `vars.error` and contain no assignments. Do not put `code=` on `uipath:error`;
347	  model the code on `bpmn:error errorCode` and reference via `errorRef`.
348	
349	## Subprocess, call activity, event subprocess (REGISTRY GAP for structure)
350	
351	- **SubProcess** (`bpmn:SubProcess`): a container with its own nested
352	  `flowElements` (start event, nodes, end event) and its own scoped
353	  `<uipath:variables>`. Variants: `collapsed`, `expanded`, `eventSubprocess`.
354	  The shape carries `isExpanded` for the collapsed/expanded distinction.
355	- **Event subprocess**: a `bpmn:SubProcess` with `triggeredByEvent="true"`. It
356	  must have **exactly one** start event, and that start event **must carry an
357	  event definition** (with `isInterrupting`) — a blank start event is invalid for
358	  an event subprocess.
359	- **Call activity** (`bpmn:CallActivity`): invokes a *separate* Maestro
360	  instance. The registry provides the `uipath:activity` payload for the
361	  Orchestrator agentic/case-management call-activity types
362	  (`Orchestrator.StartAgenticProcess[Async]`, `…CaseMgmtProcess[Async]`). A
363	  plain BPMN `calledElement` round-trips but is not specially authored by the
364	  canvas layer.
365	- Each scope (process or sub-process) may have at most one blank (untyped) start
366	  event (`MULTIPLE_BLANK_START_EVENTS`).
367	
368	> SubProcess scopes operations *within the same instance*; CallActivity invokes
369	> a *separate* Maestro instance. Do not conflate them.
370	
371	## Multi-instance / loop characteristics (REGISTRY GAP — canvas supports it)
372	
373	The registry spec enumerates **no** multi-instance or loop markers
374	(`grep` for `multiInstance`/`loopCharacteristics` in `bpmn-spec.json` returns
375	nothing). This is a genuine registry gap. The Studio Web canvas, however, **does**
376	serialize them (`elements/nodes.ts`), so author them from the canvas contract:
377	
378	```xml
379	<bpmn:multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics isSequential="true">
380	  <bpmn:completionCondition xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">=vars.Var_Done</bpmn:completionCondition>
381	  <bpmn:extensionElements>
382	    <uipath:loopCharacteristics
383	        inputCollection="=vars.Var_Items" inputElement="item" />
384	  </bpmn:extensionElements>
385	</bpmn:multiInstanceLoopCharacteristics>
386	```
387	
388	- `isSequential="true"` = one at a time; `false` = parallel.
389	- The collection/item binding lives in the `uipath:loopCharacteristics`
390	  extension (`inputCollection`, `inputElement`), **not** in `loopCardinality`
391	  (the canvas never reads `loopCardinality`).
392	- The loop element **must declare `inputElement`** — do not rely on reading a
393	  bare `iterator`/`iterator.item` downstream without it. For a multi-instance
394	  **subprocess** body, bind `inputElement="iterator[0]"` on
395	  `uipath:loopCharacteristics` and pass the current item into body activities
396	  with `=iterator[0].item`. Do not assume a bare alias such as `=currentItem` is
397	  in scope inside a marker subprocess body unless the file already uses it.
398	- Inside the body, read the current item with the `iterator` namespace — see
399	  [expression-authoring.md](expression-authoring.md).
400	- `bpmn:standardLoopCharacteristics` is also recognized (no uipath extension).
401	
402	Because the registry exposes no template for this, treat it as a documented
403	authoring path backed by the canvas serializer, and tell the user it is a
404	registry gap if they ask why no `registry get` covers it.
405	
406	## Do not generate for new authoring (preserve on round-trip only)
407	
408	These structures are **not** authored for new Maestro BPMN. If they appear in an
409	imported or brownfield file, preserve them and report that the skill cannot
410	safely regenerate or normalize them. Planned / preview / TBD statuses count as
411	unsupported for generation until current tooling confirms them.
412	
413	- Gateway: `bpmn:complexGateway`.
414	- Tasks / containers: `bpmn:manualTask`, `bpmn:adHocSubProcess`,
415	  `bpmn:transaction`.
416	- Event definitions: `conditionalEventDefinition`, `signalEventDefinition`,
417	  `escalationEventDefinition`, `compensateEventDefinition`,
418	  `cancelEventDefinition`, `linkEventDefinition`, multiple, and
419	  parallel-multiple event definitions.
420	- Markers: standard-loop and compensation markers (use only documented
421	  multi-instance parallel/sequential metadata for new loops).
422	- Terminate is supported **only** on end events — not on start, boundary,
423	  intermediate-catch, or intermediate-throw events.
424	- Preserve-only `uipath:*` extension payloads: keep these when imported, and when
425	  a file legitimately needs one, reproduce the shape (with synthetic, public-safe
426	  contents) rather than inventing a new one.
427	  - **Typed activity/event shells always use the lowercase `<uipath:activity>` /
428	    `<uipath:event>` wrapper with a `<uipath:type value="<Type>" version="v1" />`
429	    child** — including types not served by the live registry (e.g.
430	    `Maestro.CasePlanScheduler`, `Maestro.CaseManagerGuardrails`,
431	    `Maestro.CaseRulesEvaluator`). Do **not** substitute the capital-`A`
432	    `<uipath:Activity>` element for a typed shell.
433	  - The capital-`A` `<uipath:Activity>` element is a **separate** generic
434	    preserve-only payload (its own element, not a wrapper for typed shells). If
435	    a prompt asks for a generic unsupported `uipath:Activity`, preserve that
436	    exact capitalized tag, for example:
437	    `<uipath:Activity version="v1"><uipath:type value="uipath:Activity" version="v1" /></uipath:Activity>`.
438	    Do not encode it as lowercase `<uipath:activity>` with
439	    `<uipath:type value="uipath:Activity" />`; that misses the preserve-only
440	    payload shape.
441	  - `uipath:caseManagement` is a versioned body-string element —
442	    `<uipath:caseManagement version="v1">…synthetic payload…</uipath:caseManagement>`.
443	    If a prompt asks for case-management contract variants, preserve-only
444	    case-management payloads, or case-plan/case-management wrappers, include an
445	    actual lowercase `uipath:caseManagement` element with synthetic content. A
446	    typed `Orchestrator.StartCaseMgmtProcess*` activity shell is not the same
447	    payload and does not satisfy that preserve-only case-management shape.
448	  - `<uipath:scriptVersion value="v2" />` is legacy: author `v3` for new scripts,
449	    preserve `v2` where it already exists.
450	
451	## Diagram interchange — `bpmndi` (REGISTRY GAP — always generated)
452	
453	The registry emits no diagram. Import is **diagram-driven**: the canvas builds
454	nodes from `BPMNShape`s and edges from `BPMNEdge`s, not by walking
455	`flowElements`. **A node with no shape is invisible; a flow with no edge is
456	dropped.** You must generate the full `BPMNDiagram` yourself.
457	
458	- One `<bpmndi:BPMNShape id="S_<nodeId>" bpmnElement="<nodeId>">` per node, with
459	  `<dc:Bounds x= y= width= height= />`. SubProcess shapes carry `isExpanded`.
460	- One `<bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="BPMNEdge_<flowId>" bpmnElement="<flowId>">` per
461	  sequence flow, with `<di:waypoint x= y= />` points.
462	- Lay nodes out left-to-right with non-overlapping bounds. Typical sizes: tasks
463	  100×80, events 36×36, gateways 50×50.
464	
465	Example:
466	
467	```xml
468	<bpmndi:BPMNShape id="S_StartEvent_1" bpmnElement="StartEvent_1">
469	  <dc:Bounds x="160" y="100" width="36" height="36" />
470	</bpmndi:BPMNShape>
471	<bpmndi:BPMNEdge id="BPMNEdge_Flow_1" bpmnElement="Flow_1">
472	  <di:waypoint x="196" y="118" />
473	  <di:waypoint x="260" y="118" />
474	</bpmndi:BPMNEdge>
475	```
476	
477	## Editing operations
478	
479	Safe, surgical edits on an existing `.bpmn` (preserve content you did not author
480	— see [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md#editing-an-existing-bpmn-preserve-what-you-did-not-author)):
481	
482	- **Add / delete / reconnect a node**: add the element with a stable id and its
483	  `<bpmn:incoming>`/`<bpmn:outgoing>` refs, add the sequence-flow elements in the
484	  owning scope, and add/update its `BPMNShape` and edge waypoints. On delete,
485	  remove orphaned flows and DI edges and recheck entry-point variables, output
486	  mappings, and binding references.
487	- **Insert a gateway**: split the existing sequence flow into an incoming and an
488	  outgoing flow, add conditions to the outgoing flows plus one `default`, add a
489	  matching join only if branches actually need synchronization, then re-waypoint
490	  the diagram (gateway shape + all edges).
491	- **Move logic into a subprocess**: move only elements that share a valid scope,
492	  re-scope their variables, recreate legal subprocess flow boundaries, and add a
493	  second diagram plane for the subprocess so nested content renders.
494	- **Add an entry point**: use a root-level start event, add a stable unique
495	  `uipath:entryPointId`, and declare input/output variables whose `elementId`
496	  matches that start event.
497	
498	Do not patch generated JSON to fix source behavior — change the `.bpmn` and
499	regenerate. For `Intsvc.*` activities/triggers, hand editing to CLI enrichment.
500	
501	### Edit red-flags
502	
503	Re-check after any edit:
504	
505	- A diagram plane references a missing process, collaboration, or subprocess.
506	- A rendered element lacks a shape or its flow lacks an edge/waypoint.
507	- An entry-point variable points at the wrong start event.
508	- A `uipath:context` value references a missing binding.
509	- A topology edit rewrote unrelated `uipath:*` extension XML.
510	- An Integration Service element carries hand-authored connection details.
511	
512	## Validation
513	
514	Validate with the CLI — it runs the full PO.Frontend canvas rule set offline
515	(the same Node/Edge/CanvasState reconstruction and every canvas rule), plus the
516	deploy-readiness checks:
517	
518	```bash
519	uip maestro bpmn validate <file.bpmn> --output json
520	```
521	
522	Exit 0 means the document passes all rules. Exit 1 lists the blocking errors,
523	each with its rule code (gateway/condition, fake-join, superfluous-gateway,
524	error end/boundary event, timer-duration/required-field, single-blank-start,
525	single-conditional-outgoing-flow, variable-reference, method-parentheses,
526	input-type, event-object, and IS-connector checks). Warnings are reported but do
527	not block. If `validate` is unknown or runs only deploy-readiness checks, update
528	the CLI — see [cli-conventions.md](cli-conventions.md#discovery-commands-read-only-authoring-safe).
529	
530	If the CLI is unavailable, fall back to a well-formed-XML parse plus the
531	structural checklist below — it mirrors the same blocking rules:
532	
533	```bash
534	python3 -c "import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET; ET.parse('<file.bpmn>')"
535	```
536	
537	Then walk the structural checklist:
538	
539	1. Root is `<…:definitions>` with the BPMN + `uipath` namespaces.
540	2. Exactly one `<bpmndi:BPMNDiagram>` with a shape per node and an edge per flow.
541	3. Every `sourceRef`/`targetRef`/`attachedToRef`/`*Ref` resolves to a declared id.
542	4. Each XOR gateway: non-default flows have conditions; exactly one default.
543	5. No activity/event has more than one incoming flow.
544	6. Each event subprocess has exactly one start event, and it carries an event
545	   definition (with `isInterrupting`).
546	7. Every `vars.<id>` reference resolves to a declared variable.
547	8. Each `uipath:*` payload was produced from a `registry get` template, not
548	   hand-written.

152	- **Connector activity** (`Intsvc.ActivityExecution` / a connector-authenticated
153	  operation): use when the call goes through a tenant connection, a dynamic
154	  connector schema, or a connector object operation. Keep the node **draft**
155	  until enriched. The CLI-owned enrichment blockers — the ones that must be
156	  resolved before upload or run, and that boundary notes should name explicitly
157	  — are **connection binding**, **dynamic schemas**, generated **package
158	  metadata** (`bindings_v2.json`, `entry-points.json`, `operate.json`,
159	  `package-descriptor.json`). Do not hand-author any of these (§3).
160	- **Connectionless / manual HTTP** (`Intsvc.HttpExecution`, or
161	  `Intsvc.UnifiedHttpRequest` when current tooling exposes the unified shape):
162	  use when the workflow itself owns the URL, method, payload, and response
163	  parsing (no connection). Author `mode="manual"`, `method`, `url`, `headers`,
164	  `parameters`, `body` directly from the registry template.
165	
166	Status vocabulary for an IS node in a summary: **executable** (activity, inputs,
167	output variable, and downstream mappings present, runtime-verified if a run was
168	done), **draft** (BPMN shape/intent present but enrichment missing), **mock**
169	(returns fixed sample data instead of calling out), **blocked** (a required URL,
170	auth, schema, or enrichment decision is missing).
171	
172	## 5. Assemble
173	
174	1. Build the document scaffold and process (see
175	   [structural-bpmn.md](structural-bpmn.md)).
176	2. Declare root variables (`BPMN.Variables` template) and the
177	   `<uipath:bindings>` block.
178	3. For each node, paste its `registry get` `xmlTemplate`, fill placeholders, and
179	   wire `{incomingEdge}`/`{outgoingEdge}` to your sequence flows.
180	4. Author the structural BPMN the registry does not emit: sequence flows,
181	   gateway conditions/defaults, event definitions, boundary events,
182	   subprocess/call-activity containers, multi-instance markers.
183	5. Generate the `bpmndi:BPMNDiagram` (shape per node, edge per flow).
184	6. Validate (see [structural-bpmn.md#validation](structural-bpmn.md#validation)).
185

1	# HITL AppTask Node — Direct JSON Reference
2	
3	The AppTask variant uses a deployed coded app (Studio Web) as the task form. Node type: `uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app`. Same three handles (`input`, `completed`) as QuickForm. Difference from QuickForm: `inputs.app` points to the deployed app (no inline schema).
4	
5	---
6	
7	## App Lookup and Solution Registration
8	
9	Before writing the node JSON, resolve the app and register it with the solution. All API calls use auth from the stored login session (`uip login`).
10	
11	### Step 1 — Resolve solution context and credentials
12	
13	**Read credentials from the active `uip` session:**
14	
15	```bash
16	source "$HOME/.uipath/.auth"
17	# Variables now available:
18	# UIPATH_ACCESS_TOKEN       — bearer token
19	# UIPATH_URL                — e.g. https://cloud.uipath.com
20	# UIPATH_ORGANIZATION_NAME  — org name (slug)
21	# UIPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID    — org UUID
22	# UIPATH_TENANT_NAME
23	# UIPATH_TENANT_ID
24	# UIPATH_PROJECT_ID
25	```
26	
27	Map to working variables:
28	
29	| Variable | Source |
30	|---|---|
31	| `BASE_URL` | `$UIPATH_URL` |
32	| `ORG_NAME` | `$UIPATH_ORGANIZATION_NAME` |
33	| `ORG_ID` | `$UIPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID` |
34	| `TENANT_ID` | `$UIPATH_TENANT_ID` |
35	| `ACCESS_TOKEN` | `$UIPATH_ACCESS_TOKEN` |
36	| `USER_ID` | `sub` claim — base64url-decode the middle segment of `ACCESS_TOKEN`, parse JSON, read `sub` |
37	
38	**Resolve solution context:**
39	
40	Find the `.uipx` file: look in the flow file's directory first, then its parent directory.
41	
42	Parse it as JSON:
43	
44	```json
45	{
46	  "SolutionId": "<SOLUTION_ID>",
47	  "Projects": [
48	    { "Id": "<PROJECT_KEY>", "ProjectRelativePath": "<ProjectName>/<ProjectName>.uiproj" }
49	  ]
50	}
51	```
52	
53	Extract `SolutionId` → `SOLUTION_ID`. Find the entry in `Projects[]` whose directory matches the flow file's directory → its `Id` is `PROJECT_KEY`.
54	
55	> If no project entry matches, the project is not registered. Run `uip solution projects add` first.
56	
57	### Step 2 — Search for apps
58	
59	```
60	GET {BASE_URL}/{ORG_NAME}/studio_/backend/api/resourcebuilder/solutions/{SOLUTION_ID}/resources/search
61	  ?kind=app
62	  &pageSize=25
63	  &projectKey={PROJECT_KEY}
64	  &includeSolutionResources=true
65	  &types=VB%20Action
66	  &types=Workflow%20Action
67	  &types=Coded%20Action
68	  &types=CodedAction
69	  &searchTerm={APP_NAME}
70	```
71	
72	Headers: `Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}`, `Accept: application/json`, `x-uipath-tenantid: {TENANT_ID}`
73	
74	Response:
75	
76	```json
77	{
78	  "solutionResources": [
79	    {
80	      "fullyQualifiedName": "Shared",
81	      "path": "Shared",
82	      "key": "<folderKey>",
83	      "resources": [
84	        { "key": "<appKey>", "name": "Invoice Approval", "type": "Coded Action", "kind": "app" }
85	      ]
86	    }
87	  ],
88	  "availableResources": [...],
89	  "nextPageCursor": null
90	}
91	```
92	
93	If this returns 401, upload the solution uipx file first by just using the solution-tool cli upload command, do not bundle the solution.
94	
95	Flatten both `solutionResources` and `availableResources` folder groups into a single list. Each item carries: `key`, `name`, `type`, `kind`, and its parent `folder` (`fullyQualifiedName`, `path`, `folderKey`).
96	
97	**Selection rules:**
98	
99	- **Exactly one match** → use it, proceed to Step 3.
100	- **Multiple matches** → present a numbered list to the user and wait for their choice before proceeding:
101	
102	  > I found multiple apps matching that name. Which one should I use?
103	  > 1. **Invoice Approval** — Shared / Coded Action
104	  > 2. **Invoice Approval** — Finance / VB Action
105	  >
106	  > Reply with the number of the app you want.
107	
108	  Use `nextPageCursor` to fetch additional pages if the list is truncated. Do not proceed until the user selects.
109	
110	- **Zero matches** → stop and tell the user: "No deployed app named `<APP_NAME>` was found. Verify the name and that the app is deployed, then try again. Show them the app name, folder name and type"
111	
112	### Step 3 — Retrieve app configuration
113	
114	```
115	POST {BASE_URL}/{ORG_NAME}/studio_/backend/api/resourcebuilder/solutions/{SOLUTION_ID}/resources/retrieve-configuration
116	Content-Type: application/json
117	
118	{
119	  "key": "<selectedApp.key>",
120	  "name": "<selectedApp.name>",
121	  "kind": "app",
122	  "type": "<selectedApp.type>",
123	  "folder": <selectedApp.folder>
124	}
125	```
126	
127	Headers: `Authorization: Bearer {ACCESS_TOKEN}`, `Content-Type: application/json`, `Accept: application/json`, `x-uipath-tenantid: {TENANT_ID}`
128	
129	The response is a resource object. Key extractions from `spec`:
130	
131	| Extract | Field | Notes |
132	|---|---|---|
133	| `APP_SYSTEM_NAME` | `spec.appSystemName` | |
134	| `APP_VERSION_REF` | `spec.appVersionRef` | object `{ key, name }` |
135	| `VERSION` | `spec.version` | default `"1.0.0"` if absent |
136	| `inputSchema` | parsed from `spec.actionSchema` → `.inputs` | `spec.actionSchema` is a **JSON string** — parse it first |
137	| `inOutSchema` | parsed from `spec.actionSchema` → `.inOuts` | |
138	| `folder` | `raw.folder.fullyQualifiedName`, `.path`, `.folderKey` | fall back to `selectedApp.folder` values |
139	
140	> If this call fails, warn and continue with empty `inputSchema`/`inOutSchema`.
141	
142	### Step 4 — Write solution resource files
143	
144	Create directories as needed. All paths are relative to `<solutionDir>` (the directory containing the `.uipx` file).
145	
146	**File 1: `resources/solution_folder/app/<app.type>/<AppName>.json`**
147	
148	```json
149	{
150	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
151	  "resource": {
152	    "name": "<app.name>",
153	    "kind": "app",
154	    "type": "<app.type>",
155	    "apiVersion": "apps.uipath.com/v1",
156	    "isOverridable": true,
157	    "dependencies": [{ "name": "<app.name>", "kind": "appVersion" }],
158	    "runtimeDependencies": [],
159	    "files": [],
160	    "folders": [{ "fullyQualifiedName": "solution_folder" }],
161	    "spec": {
162	      "name": "<app.name>",
163	      "description": "<spec.description or null>",
164	      "type": "<spec.type or 'Regular'>",
165	      "appSystemName": "<APP_SYSTEM_NAME or app.key>",
166	      "version": "<VERSION or '1.0.0'>",
167	      "appVersionRef": "<APP_VERSION_REF or { name: app.name, key: app.key }>",
168	      "actionSchema": "<raw spec.actionSchema string — do not re-serialize>"
169	    },
170	    "locks": [],
171	    "key": "<app.key>"
172	  }
173	}
174	```
175	
176	> Write `spec.actionSchema` verbatim from the API response. Re-serializing it changes unicode escapes vs. plain quotes and will break schema matching.
177	
178	**File 2: `resources/solution_folder/appVersion/<AppName>.json`** *(skip if `APP_SYSTEM_NAME` or `APP_VERSION_REF` are absent)*
179	
180	```json
181	{
182	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
183	  "resource": {
184	    "name": "<app.name>",
185	    "kind": "appVersion",
186	    "apiVersion": "apps.uipath.com/v1",
187	    "isOverridable": true,
188	    "dependencies": [],
189	    "runtimeDependencies": [],
190	    "files": [
191	      {
192	        "name": "<app.name>.uiapp",
193	        "kind": "appVersion",
194	        "url": "<BASE_URL>/<ORG_ID>/apps_/default/api/v1/default/models/<APP_SYSTEM_NAME>/publish/versions/<MAJOR_VERSION>/package",
195	        "key": "<APP_VERSION_REF.key>"
196	      }
197	    ],
198	    "folders": [],
199	    "spec": {
200	      "name": "<app.name>",
201	      "description": "",
202	      "appSystemName": "<APP_SYSTEM_NAME>",
203	      "version": "<VERSION or '1.0.0'>",
204	      "isAppPublic": false,
205	      "expressionLanguage": null,
206	      "publishNote": null,
207	      "uiappFile": "<APP_VERSION_REF.key>",
208	      "uiappFileName": "<app.name>.uiapp",
209	      "isUnifiedProject": null
210	    },
211	    "locks": [],
212	    "key": "<APP_VERSION_REF.key>"
213	  }
214	}
215	```
216	
217	`MAJOR_VERSION` = first segment of `VERSION` (e.g. `"2.0.1"` → `"2"`).
218	
219	### Step 5 — Register app reference
220	
221	```
222	POST {BASE_URL}/{ORG_NAME}/studio_/backend/api/resourcebuilder/solutions/{SOLUTION_ID}/resources/reference?api-version=2&forceUpdate=true
223	Content-Type: application/json
224	
225	{
226	  "kind": "app",
227	  "type": "<app.type>",
228	  "key": "<app.key>",
229	  "folder": {
230	    "fullyQualifiedName": "<folder.fullyQualifiedName>",
231	    "path": "<folder.path>",
232	    "folderKey": "<folder.folderKey>"
233	  }
234	}
235	```
236	
237	> If this call fails, warn and continue.
238	
239	### Step 6 — Write debug overwrites
240	
241	Read `<solutionDir>/userProfile/<USER_ID>/debug_overwrites.json` if it exists. Merge in the new entry — do not overwrite unrelated entries.
242	
243	Structure:
244	
245	```json
246	{
247	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
248	  "tenants": [
249	    {
250	      "tenantKey": "<TENANT_ID>",
251	      "resources": [
252	        {
253	          "solutionResourceKey": "<app.key>",
254	          "reprovisioningIndex": 0,
255	          "overwrite": {
256	            "resourceKey": "<app.key>",
257	            "resourceName": "<app.name>",
258	            "folderKey": "<folder.folderKey>",
259	            "folderFullyQualifiedName": "<folder.fullyQualifiedName>",
260	            "folderPath": "<folder.path>",
261	            "type": "Reference",
262	            "kind": "app"
263	          }
264	        }
265	      ]
266	    }
267	  ]
268	}

270	
271	Merge rules:
272	- Tenant entry for `TENANT_ID` exists → find resource by `solutionResourceKey` and replace, or append if not found.
273	- No tenant entry → add a new tenant object.
274	
275	> If this write fails, warn and continue.

285	  "typeVersion": "1.0",

344

1	# HITL QuickForm Node — Direct JSON Reference
2	
3	The agent writes the `uipath.human-in-the-loop.quick-form` node directly into the `.flow` file as JSON. **Direct JSON is the default.** A CLI opt-in is available when the user explicitly requests it, or as a fallback if direct JSON writing fails — see [CLI reference: uip maestro flow hitl add](../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-hitl-add).
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Step 1 — Extract the Schema Through Conversation
8	
9	Before designing the schema, ask these focused questions if the business description doesn't answer them. **Ask all missing ones in a single message — never one at a time.** **Running non-interactively (CI/headless — no user available to answer):** do not ask — infer the answers from the prompt and any upstream `.flow` data, and proceed to design the schema. Only stop and report the open decision if the request is too ambiguous to pick a sensible default.
10	
11	| What you need to know | Question to ask |
12	|---|---|
13	| What the reviewer sees | "What information does the reviewer need to make their decision?" |
14	| What they fill in | "Does the reviewer need to enter any data, or just click Approve/Reject?" |
15	| What actions they take | "What are the named actions — e.g. Approve/Reject, or something domain-specific like Accept/Negotiate/Decline?" |
16	
17	**Common business descriptions → schema translations:**
18	
19	| Business description | Schema shape |
20	|---|---|
21	| "Human reviews and approves/rejects an invoice" | `inputs: [invoiceId, amount]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |
22	| "Reviewer checks agent-drafted email before sending" | `inputs: [draftEmail, recipientName]`, `inOuts: [emailBody]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |
23	| "Escalate to human when confidence < 0.7" | `inputs: [agentReasoning, confidenceScore]`, `outputs: [action, notes]`, `outcomes: [Retry, Skip, Escalate]` |
24	| "Human fills in missing vendor data" | `inputs: [rawExtract]`, `outputs: [vendorName, costCenter]`, `outcomes: [Submit]` |
25	| "Approve before writing to ServiceNow" | `inputs: [proposedChange, targetSystem]`, `inOuts: [finalValue]`, `outcomes: [Approve, Reject]` |
26	
27	---
28	
29	## Step 1b — Discover Upstream Variables
30	
31	Before designing input field bindings, read **both** `workflow.variables.nodes` and `workflow.variables.globals` from the `.flow` file.
32	
33	### Node outputs (`variables.nodes`)
34	
35	Each entry exposes exactly what `$vars` paths are available:
36	
37	```json
38	{ "id": "fetchInvoice.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "fetchInvoice", "outputId": "output" } }
39	```
40	
41	The `id` field is the `$vars` path — `fetchInvoice.output` → `$vars.fetchInvoice.output`. Nested field access appends `.fieldName` (e.g., `$vars.fetchInvoice.output.invoiceId`).
42	
43	> **Binding path key = upstream script output key, not the HITL field `id`.** The HITL field `id` identifies the form field (lowercase, used for rendering). The binding path key is the property name in the upstream script's `return` statement. These are different things. If the script returns `{ supplierName: "Acme" }` and you give the HITL field `"id": "suppliername"`, the correct binding is `vars.fetchSupplier.output.supplierName` — NOT `vars.fetchSupplier.output.suppliername`. The field `id` is irrelevant to the binding path. Always look at the upstream script source to derive the key, never at the HITL field schema you are writing.
44	
45	**outputId by node type:**
46	
47	| Node type | outputId | Access pattern |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| HTTP node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.body.{field}` |
50	| Script node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{field}` |
51	| Prior HITL node | `output`, `status` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.{field}` |
52	| Agent node | `output` | `$vars.{nodeId}.output.content` |
53	| Trigger (manual) | `output` | `$vars.start.output.{field}` |
54	
55	### Flow-level globals (`variables.globals`)
56	
57	Also read `workflow.variables.globals`. Each entry has an `id` that maps directly to a `$vars` reference — no node prefix, no `.output` segment:
58	
59	```json
60	{ "id": "customerName", "direction": "in", "type": "string" }
61	```
62	
63	→ HITL binding: `"vars.customerName"` (no `=js:$` prefix — HITL binding is a raw path)
64	
65	**When to use globals instead of node outputs:** When data was declared as a flow-level input variable (e.g. the trigger passes it as a named parameter via `triggerNodeId`), it lives in `globals` with `direction: "in"`. Bind directly to `vars.<globalId>` — do not add `.output` or a node prefix.
66	
67	| Source | HITL `binding` format | Expression format (other nodes) |
68	|---|---|---|
69	| Node output | `vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>` | `=js:$vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>` |
70	| Flow global (`direction: "in"`) | `vars.<globalId>` | `=js:$vars.<globalId>` |
71	
72	> **`binding` vs `variable` prefix rule:** `binding` (input/inOut fields) uses the full path starting with `vars.` because it references an existing variable path. `variable` (output/inOut fields) uses `vars.<name>` — the `vars.` prefix is required; it declares the global variable name.
73	
74	For the full variable system, see → [How $vars paths are constructed in Flow](../../uipath-maestro-flow/references/shared/variables-and-expressions.md)
75	
76	---
77	
78	## Step 2 — Design the Schema
79	
80	The node schema uses `fields[]` entries inside `inputs.schema`. Use these conceptual roles to plan the fields before writing the node JSON:
81	
82	| Role | `direction` value | Human can… | Use for |
83	|---|---|---|---|
84	| Input field | `"input"` | Read only | Context the human needs to make a decision |
85	| Output field | `"output"` | Write | Data the automation needs back |
86	| InOut field | `"inOut"` | Read + modify | Data the human can see and optionally correct |
87	
88	**Supported field types:** `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `file`
89	
90	**Design rules:**
91	- Input fields: everything the human needs to decide — IDs, amounts, context; bind to upstream node output via `binding`
92	- Output fields: only what downstream nodes actually use; set `required: true` for mandatory outputs
93	- `outcomes`: use domain-specific names (Approve/Reject, not just Submit)
94	- Keep it focused — don't add fields the automation won't use
95	
96	**Show the designed schema to the user and confirm before writing the node.** **Running non-interactively (CI/headless — no user available to answer):** do not block — design the schema from the prompt and any upstream `.flow` data, write the node, and record the chosen schema prominently in the final report. Only stop and report the open decision if the request is too ambiguous to pick a sensible default. (A prompt that already specifies the fields, outcomes, and output shape is never too ambiguous.)
97

280	
281	> **Scripts must always use `$vars.<nodeId>.output.<fieldId>`.** The `field.variable` property declares a name for the global alias — do NOT use that name directly in scripts. `$vars.decision` (global alias) and `$vars.<nodeId>.output.decision` (field ID access) are different paths and only the field ID path is reliable in script nodes. See Critical Rule 10 in SKILL.md.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## Canonical Field Shape (reference)
286	
287	This is the exact JSON a correctly authored QuickForm `fields[]` entry looks like for each direction. Use this as ground truth when writing or reviewing HITL nodes.
288	
289	```json
290	{
291	  "fields": [
292	    {
293	      "id": "invoiceid",
294	      "type": "number",
295	      "label": "Invoice ID",
296	      "direction": "input",
297	      "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice1.output.invoiceId"
298	    },
299	    {
300	      "id": "vendorname",
301	      "type": "string",
302	      "label": "Vendor Name",
303	      "direction": "input",
304	      "binding": "vars.fetchInvoice1.output.vendorName"
305	    },
306	    {
307	      "id": "approveddate",
308	      "type": "date",
309	      "label": "Approved Date",
310	      "direction": "output",
311	      "variable": "vars.approvedDate"
312	    },
313	    {
314	      "id": "approved",
315	      "type": "boolean",
316	      "label": "Approved",
317	      "direction": "output",
318	      "variable": "vars.approved"
319	    }
320	  ],
321	  "outcomes": [
322	    {
323	      "id": "submit",
324	      "name": "Submit",
325	      "type": "string",
326	      "action": "Continue",
327	      "isPrimary": true
328	    }
329	  ]
330	}
331	```
332	
333	**Key rules this sample encodes:**
334	- `type`: always a JS/JSON type — `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, or `file`. Never `"text"`.
335	- `variable`: always `"vars.<name>"` — the `vars.` prefix is required.
336	- `binding`: input/inOut fields only; raw path (`vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>`), no `=js:$` prefix.
337	- Output/inOut fields have `variable`; input fields do not.
338	
339	---
340	
341	## Schema Conversion — Examples
342	
343	The agent translates the user's business description into the `fields[]` and `outcomes[]` arrays. No CLI needed — apply these rules directly.
344	
345	### Rules
346	
347	| What | Rule |
348	|---|---|
349	| field `id` | lowercase label, spaces→`-`, strip non-alphanumeric. `"Invoice ID"` → `"invoiceid"`, `"Due Date"` → `"due-date"` |
350	| `direction` | `inputs[]` items → `"input"`, `outputs[]` → `"output"`, `inOuts[]` → `"inOut"` |
351	| field `type` | Use the JS/JSON type: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, or `file` |
352	| `binding` | **Input / inOut fields only.** Format: `"vars.<nodeId>.output.<field>"` for node outputs; `"vars.<globalId>"` for flow globals. **No `=js:$` prefix** — HITL binding is a raw path, not an expression. |
353	| `variable` | **Output / inOut fields only** — absent on input fields. Format: `"vars.<name>"` (always include the `vars.` prefix). Defaults to `"vars.<camelCase id>"` if not specified. |
354	| `required` | omit if false; set `true` for mandatory outputs |
355	| `outcomes[0]` | `isPrimary: true`, `action: "Continue"` |
356	| `outcomes[1+]` | `isPrimary: false`, `action: "End"` |
357	| `schema.schemaId` | Generate a fresh UUID (e.g. `crypto.randomUUID()` or any UUID v4) |
358	
359	### Example 1 — Simple approval (inputs only + outcomes)
360	
361	Business description: *"Reviewer sees invoice ID and amount, clicks Approve or Reject"*
362	
363	```json
364	"fields": [
365	  { "id": "invoiceid", "label": "Invoice ID", "type": "string",   "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchData1.output.invoiceId" },
366	  { "id": "amount",    "label": "Amount",     "type": "number", "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.fetchData1.output.amount" }
367	],
368	"outcomes": [
369	  { "id": "approve", "name": "Approve", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true,  "action": "Continue" },
370	  { "id": "reject",  "name": "Reject",  "type": "string", "isPrimary": false, "action": "End" }
371	]
372	```
373	
374	### Example 2 — Write-back validation (inOut — human can edit before confirming)
375	
376	Business description: *"Human sees the AI-drafted email, can edit it, then clicks Send or Discard"*
377	
378	```json
379	"fields": [
380	  { "id": "recipient",  "label": "Recipient",  "type": "string", "direction": "input", "binding": "vars.draft1.output.recipient" },
381	  { "id": "emailbody",  "label": "Email Body", "type": "string", "direction": "inOut", "binding": "vars.draft1.output.body", "variable": "vars.emailBody" }
382	],
383	"outcomes": [
384	  { "id": "send",    "name": "Send",    "type": "string", "isPrimary": true,  "action": "Continue" },
385	  { "id": "discard", "name": "Discard", "type": "string", "isPrimary": false, "action": "End" }
386	]
387	```
388	
389	### Example 3 — Data enrichment (output — human fills in missing fields)
390	
391	Business description: *"Agent couldn't extract vendor name or cost center. Human fills them in and clicks Submit."*
392	
393	```json
394	"fields": [
395	  { "id": "rawextract",  "label": "Raw Extract",  "type": "string", "direction": "input",  "binding": "vars.extract1.output.rawText" },
396	  { "id": "vendorname",  "label": "Vendor Name",  "type": "string", "direction": "output", "variable": "vars.vendorName",  "required": true },
397	  { "id": "costcenter",  "label": "Cost Center",  "type": "string", "direction": "output", "variable": "vars.costCenter", "required": true }
398	],
399	"outcomes": [
400	  { "id": "submit", "name": "Submit", "type": "string", "isPrimary": true, "action": "Continue" }
401	]
402	```
403	
404	### Example 4 — Exception escalation (multiple outcomes + notes output)
405	
406	Business description: *"If agent confidence is low, escalate. Human sees reasoning and score, can Retry, Skip, or Escalate further."*
407	
408	```json
409	"fields": [
410	  { "id": "reasoning",       "label": "Agent Reasoning",  "type": "string",   "direction": "input",  "binding": "vars.classify1.output.reasoning" },
411	  { "id": "confidencescore", "label": "Confidence Score", "type": "number", "direction": "input",  "binding": "vars.classify1.output.score" },
412	  { "id": "notes",           "label": "Notes",            "type": "string",   "direction": "output", "variable": "vars.notes" }
413	],
414	"outcomes": [
415	  { "id": "retry",    "name": "Retry",    "type": "string", "isPrimary": true,  "action": "Continue" },
416	  { "id": "skip",     "name": "Skip",     "type": "string", "isPrimary": false, "action": "End" },
417	  { "id": "escalate", "name": "Escalate", "type": "string", "isPrimary": false, "action": "End" }
418	]
419	```
420	
421	> **`outcomeType` for middle outcomes:** Use `"Neutral"` when the outcome is neither clearly positive nor negative (e.g., Skip, Defer, Hold).
422	
423	---
424	
425	## Runtime Variables
426	
427	After the HITL node, downstream nodes can reference:
428	
429	| Variable | Type | What it contains |
430	|---|---|---|
431	| `$vars.<nodeId>.output` | object | All `output` and `inOut` field values keyed by **field `id`** |
432	| `$vars.<nodeId>.output.<fieldId>` | varies | Individual field value using the field's `id` (e.g. `$vars.invoiceReview1.output.decision`) |
433	| `$vars.<nodeId>.status` | string | Selected outcome name (e.g. `"Approve"`, `"Reject"`) |
434	| `$vars.<globalId>` | varies | Workflow-global variable for output/inOut fields. `globalId` is `field.variable` with `vars.` stripped (e.g. `variable: "vars.notes"` → `$vars.notes`). **Do not use this path in scripts — use `$vars.<nodeId>.output.<fieldId>` instead.** |
435	
436	> **`fieldId` not `variable`**: The output object properties are keyed by the field's `id` (e.g. `"decision"`), not by the `variable` property. The `variable` property (`"approvalResult"`) creates a separate workflow-global variable (`$vars.approvalResult`) — it does not change the key used in the output object. If a field has `"id": "dec1"` and `"variable": "vars.approvalResult"`, access it via the object as `$vars.nodeId.output.dec1`, or directly as `$vars.approvalResult`.
437	>
438	> **Common mistake:** A field with `"id": "approved"` and `"variable": "vars.legalApproval"` must be read as `$vars.<nodeId>.output.approved` — **not** `$vars.<nodeId>.output.legalApproval`. Using the `variable` name as the key produces `undefined` at runtime; `flow validate` does not catch it.
439	
440	**In a downstream script node** — always access inline using `$vars.<nodeId>.output.<fieldId>`, not by destructuring:
441	```javascript
442	// Correct — field ID inline access
443	const vendorName = $vars.invoiceReview1.output.vendorName;
444	const costCenter = $vars.invoiceReview1.output.costCenter;
445	if ($vars.invoiceReview1.status === "approve") {
446	  await updateSystem(vendorName, costCenter);
447	}
448	// Wrong — do NOT destructure first:
449	// const output = $vars.invoiceReview1.output;  // then output.vendorName misses the node path
450	```
451

1	# HITL Coded Action App (Inline) — Project Scaffold and Node Reference
2	
3	Create a new coded action app project inside the solution using the user's own source code, then wire the HITL node to reference it.
4	
5	Use this path when the user selects **New Coded Action App** in Step 3.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Overview
10	
11	| Step | Action |
12	|---|---|
13	| 1 | Generate keys |
14	| 2 | Create project folder and copy source code (excluding `node_modules`) |
15	| 3 | Add project to solution via CLI |
16	| 4 | Write solution resource files |
17	| 5 | Write HITL node into the `.flow` file |
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Step 1 — Generate Keys
22	
23	Generate three UUIDs before writing any files. All three are used across multiple files — generate them once and reuse.
24	
25	```bash
26	node -e "
27	const { randomUUID: r } = require('crypto');
28	console.log('APP_KEY=' + r());
29	console.log('PACKAGE_KEY=' + r());
30	console.log('PROJECT_KEY=' + r());
31	"
32	```
33	
34	| Variable | Used in |
35	|---|---|
36	| `APP_KEY` | Resource file key, HITL node `inputs.app.key` |
37	| `PACKAGE_KEY` | Package resource key, app resource `spec.package.key` |
38	| `PROJECT_KEY` | `projectKey` in both resource files |

41	
42	## Step 2 — Create Project Folder and Copy Source Code
43	
44	Create this structure relative to `<SOLUTION_DIR>` (the directory containing the `.uipx` file):

46	```
47	<SOLUTION_DIR>/
48	└── <APP_NAME>/
49	    ├── project.uiproj
50	    ├── webAppManifest.json
51	    └── source/          ← contents copied from <SOURCE_PATH> provided by the user

54	### `<APP_NAME>/project.uiproj`
55	
56	```json
57	{
58	  "ProjectType": "AppV2",
59	  "WebAppSettings": {
60	    "AppId": null,
61	    "IsCoreProject": false
62	  },
63	  "Name": "<APP_NAME>",
64	  "Description": null,
65	  "MainFile": null
66	}

68	
69	### `<APP_NAME>/webAppManifest.json`

71	```json
72	{
73	  "type": "Coded",
74	  "solutionResourceSubType": "CodedAction",
75	  "config": {
76	    "isCompiled": true,
77	    "isActionApp": true,
78	    "bundlePath": "source/dist"
79	  }
80	}

84	
85	The source path provided by the user must already contain the built `dist/` folder. Copy its contents into `<APP_NAME>/source/`, skipping `node_modules`:

95	## Step 3 — Add Project to Solution

97	```bash

105	---
106	
107	## Step 4 — Write Solution Resource Files
108	
109	Create directories as needed. All paths are relative to `<SOLUTION_DIR>`.
110	
111	### 4a — Read and transform `action-schema.json`
112	
113	Read `<SOURCE_PATH>/action-schema.json`. The file has this top-level shape:
114	
115	```json
116	{
117	  "inputs":   { "type": "object", "properties": { ... } },
118	  "outputs":  { "type": "object", "properties": { ... } },
119	  "inOuts":   { "type": "object", "properties": { ... } },
120	  "outcomes": { "type": "object", "properties": { ... } }
121	}
122	```
123	
124	Transform it into a `ParsedActionSchema` object using the algorithm below. This object is used in two places: JSON-stringified into `spec.actionSchema` in the resource file, and directly as `inputSchema`/`inOutSchema` arrays in the HITL node.
125	
126	**Transform each property in `inputs.properties`, `outputs.properties`, and `inOuts.properties`:**
127	
128	For each `{ propertyKey: propDef }` entry:
129	
130	```json
131	{
132	  "name": "<propertyKey>",
133	  "key": "<new UUID>",
134	  "required": "<propDef.required ?? false>",
135	  "version": 0,
136	  "typeNamespace": "system",
137	  "isList": "<propDef.type === 'array'>",
138	  "collectionDataType": "<'Array' if array, else null>",
139	  "type": "<mapped .NET type — see table>",
140	  "properties": "<[] for scalars; recurse for object/array-of-object>"
141	}
142	```
143	
144	For arrays (`propDef.type === "array"`): use `propDef.items.type` and `propDef.items.format` to determine the .NET type; recurse on `propDef.items.properties` if the item type is `"object"`.
145	For objects (`propDef.type === "object"`): recurse on `propDef.properties`.
146	
147	**Type mapping** (`itemType` = `propDef.type` for scalars, `propDef.items.type` for arrays; `itemFormat` = `propDef.format` or `propDef.items.format`):
148	
149	| Condition | .NET type |
150	|---|---|
151	| `itemFormat === "uuid"` | `System.Guid` |
152	| `itemFormat === "date"` | `System.DateOnly` |
153	| `itemType === "string"` | `System.String` |
154	| `itemType === "integer"` | `System.Int64` |
155	| `itemType === "number"` | `System.Decimal` |
156	| `itemType === "boolean"` | `System.Boolean` |
157	| `itemType === "object"` | `System.Object` |
158	| `itemType === "file"` | `UiPath.Platform.ResourceHandling.IResource` |
159	
160	**Transform each property in `outcomes.properties`:**
161	
162	```json
163	{
164	  "name": "<propertyKey>",
165	  "key": "<new UUID>",
166	  "required": false,
167	  "type": "System.String",
168	  "typeNamespace": "system",
169	  "isList": false,
170	  "collectionDataType": null,
171	  "properties": [],
172	  "version": 0
173	}
174	```
175	
176	**Assemble the final `ParsedActionSchema`:**
177	
178	```json
179	{
180	  "key": "<new UUID>",
181	  "version": 0,
182	  "description": "Action Schema",
183	  "id": "ID<new UUID with dashes removed>",
184	  "name": "ActionSchema",
185	  "inputs":   [ /* transformed inputs */ ],
186	  "outputs":  [ /* transformed outputs */ ],
187	  "inOuts":   [ /* transformed inOuts */ ],
188	  "outcomes": [ /* transformed outcomes */ ]
189	}
190	```
191	
192	Set `ACTION_SCHEMA_JSON_STRING = JSON.stringify(parsedSchema)`.
193	
194	### 4b — Read `externalClientId` from `uipath.json`
195	
196	Read `<SOURCE_PATH>/uipath.json`. Use its `clientId` field as `externalClientId` in the resource file below.
197	
198	### File: `resources/solution_folder/app/codedAction/<APP_NAME>.json`

200	```json
201	{
202	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
203	  "resource": {
204	    "name": "<APP_NAME>",
205	    "kind": "app",
206	    "type": "codedAction",
207	    "apiVersion": "apps.uipath.com/v1",
208	    "projectKey": "<PROJECT_KEY>",
209	    "isOverridable": true,
210	    "dependencies": [
211	      { "name": "<APP_NAME>", "kind": "package" }
212	    ],
213	    "runtimeDependencies": [],
214	    "files": [],
215	    "folders": [{ "fullyQualifiedName": "solution_folder" }],
216	    "spec": {
217	      "name": "<APP_NAME>",
218	      "description": null,
219	      "version": "1.0.0",
220	      "routingName": null,
221	      "appSystemName": null,
222	      "package": { "key": "<PACKAGE_KEY>" },
223	      "externalClientId": "<clientId from uipath.json>",
224	      "actionSchema": "<ACTION_SCHEMA_JSON_STRING>"
225	    },
226	    "locks": [],
227	    "key": "<APP_KEY>"

232	> `appSystemName` is `null` for a new app; the platform populates it on first deployment.
233	
234	### File: `resources/solution_folder/package/<APP_NAME>.json`

236	```json

238	  "docVersion": "1.0.0",
239	  "resource": {
240	    "name": "<APP_NAME>",
241	    "kind": "package",
242	    "apiVersion": "orchestrator.uipath.com/v1",

244	    "isOverridable": true,
245	    "dependencies": [],
246	    "runtimeDependencies": [],
247	    "files": [],
248	    "folders": [{ "fullyQualifiedName": "solution_folder" }],
249	    "spec": {
250	      "fileName": null,
251	      "fileReference": null,

253	      "description": null
254	    },

256	    "key": "<PACKAGE_KEY>"
257	  }

276	  "type": "uipath.human-in-the-loop.coded-action-app",
277	  "typeVersion": "1.0.0",
278	  "display": { "label": "<LABEL>" },

282	    "recipient": {

284	      "connections": {},
285	      "assignee": { "type": "group" }
286	    },
287	    "app": {
288	      "name": "<APP_NAME>",
289	      "key": "<APP_KEY>",
290	      "folderPath": "solution_folder",
291	      "inputSchema": [ /* ParsedActionSchema.inputs */ ],
292	      "inOutSchema": [ /* ParsedActionSchema.inOuts */ ],
293	      "appSystemName": null,
294	      "appVersionRef": null
295	    },
296	    "schema": {
297	      "inputs": [],

308

1	# HITL Business Pattern Recognition Guide
2	
3	Use this guide to decide whether a business process needs a Human-in-the-Loop node, and where to place it — even when the user has not explicitly asked for one.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## When to Recommend HITL
8	
9	Look for these signals in the business description or process context:
10	
11	### Approval gate
12	The automation produces something that requires sign-off before it can proceed.
13	
14	| Signal phrases | Examples |
15	|---|---|
16	| "approve", "sign off", "authorize", "get approval" | Invoice approval, PO sign-off, budget authorization |
17	| "four-eyes check", "dual control", "maker-checker" | Financial transactions, compliance workflows |
18	| "review before posting", "validate before sending" | CRM updates, email campaigns, database writes |
19	
20	**Insertion point:** After the automation generates the artifact to review, before it takes the action requiring approval.
21	
22	---
23	
24	### Exception escalation
25	The automation hits a case it cannot resolve autonomously and needs a human decision.
26	
27	| Signal phrases | Examples |
28	|---|---|
29	| "if uncertain / low confidence, escalate" | AI agent confidence threshold |
30	| "edge case", "anomaly", "exception handling" | Fraud alerts, out-of-policy transactions |
31	| "escalate to manager / supervisor" | Customer service workflows |
32	
33	**Insertion point:** Inside a conditional branch where the automation detects it cannot proceed alone.
34	
35	---
36	
37	### Data enrichment
38	The automation extracted or generated data that is incomplete — a human must fill in the gaps.
39	
40	| Signal phrases | Examples |
41	|---|---|
42	| "fill in missing fields", "enrich", "complete the record" | Partially extracted invoice data |
43	| "human validates / corrects" | OCR output verification |
44	| "needs human input before continuing" | Missing vendor code, unknown cost center |
45	
46	**Insertion point:** After extraction/generation, before the downstream step that requires complete data.
47	
48	---
49	
50	### Compliance and audit checkpoint
51	A regulation or internal policy requires documented human sign-off.
52	
53	| Signal phrases | Examples |
54	|---|---|
55	| "compliance", "audit trail", "regulatory sign-off" | SOX controls, GDPR consent flows |
56	| "must be reviewed by", "requires attestation" | Legal review gates, privacy impact assessments |
57	
58	**Insertion point:** At the mandated checkpoint defined by the regulation or policy.
59	
60	---
61	
62	### Write-back validation
63	An agent or automation is about to write to an external system — a human must confirm the proposed change.
64	
65	| Signal phrases | Examples |
66	|---|---|
67	| "before writing to", "before posting to", "agent writes to ServiceNow / SAP / CRM" | Any write to a system of record |
68	| "human confirms before agent acts" | Autonomous agent guard rails |
69	
70	**Insertion point:** Immediately before the write/post action.
71	
72	---
73	
74	### Agentic output review
75	An AI agent produced a document, draft, classification, or recommendation — a human must verify it before the result is used or published.
76	
77	| Signal phrases | Examples |
78	|---|---|
79	| "review AI-generated content", "human verifies before sending" | Agent-drafted emails, RCA reports, meeting summaries |
80	| "check before publishing", "validate AI output" | AI-written case notes, support ticket responses |
81	| "human in the loop for AI decisions" | Any LLM output going to a system of record or customer |
82	
83	**Insertion point:** After the agent node, before the downstream action that consumes the output.
84	
85	---
86	
87	### IT / change management approval
88	A change request or access request needs human authorization before the automation executes it.
89	
90	| Signal phrases | Examples |
91	|---|---|
92	| "CAB approval", "change request", "change window" | IT change management (ServiceNow, Jira Service Management) |
93	| "access request", "provision access", "grant permission" | Identity and access management workflows |
94	| "runbook approval", "deployment sign-off" | DevOps release gates |
95	
96	**Insertion point:** After the automation prepares the change record, before it applies the change.
97	
98	---
99	
100	### HR and offer / contract workflows
101	A document or decision with legal or HR significance must be reviewed before it is sent to a third party.
102	
103	| Signal phrases | Examples |
104	|---|---|
105	| "offer letter", "employment contract", "onboarding approval" | HR hiring workflows |
106	| "termination review", "performance decision" | HR case management |
107	| "contract terms", "counter-sign", "legal review gate" | Procurement, vendor onboarding |
108	
109	**Insertion point:** After document generation, before the document is dispatched.
110	
111	---
112	
113	### Customer communication approval
114	An automation is about to send a message on behalf of a person or brand — a human must review tone, accuracy, or content before it goes out.
115	
116	| Signal phrases | Examples |
117	|---|---|
118	| "approve before sending", "review draft email", "check before posting" | Customer support responses, marketing emails |
119	| "agent-written reply", "draft response" | Helpdesk, CRM follow-ups |
120	
121	**Insertion point:** After the draft is generated, before the send/post action.
122	
123	---
124	
125	### Financial transaction approval
126	A monetary action above a threshold or of a certain type requires human sign-off.
127	
128	| Signal phrases | Examples |
129	|---|---|
130	| "above threshold", "over limit", "exceeds budget" | PO approval, expense reimbursement over limit |
131	| "wire transfer", "payment release", "credit note" | AP/AR workflows |
132	| "price override", "discount approval" | Sales quote approval |
133	
134	**Insertion point:** After the automation determines the transaction details, before it submits the payment or posts the entry.
135	
136	---
137	
138	## When NOT to Recommend HITL
139	
140	- The process description is fully automated with no decision point (e.g. "process all invoices automatically")
141	- The human interaction is asynchronous notification only (use email/Slack activity instead)
142	- The user explicitly says no human review is needed
143	- The decision can be made by a rule or AI model with sufficient confidence
144	- The user is asking about **runtime task management** — reassigning, monitoring, cancelling, or checking the status of existing Action Center tasks. These are operational questions answered by `uip tasks` commands or the Orchestrator UI, not by adding a HITL node. A question like "how do I reassign a task sitting for 3 days?" is task administration, not automation authoring — do not recommend adding a HITL checkpoint in response.
145	
146	---
147	
148	## Proactive HITL Recommendation
149	
150	If a business description contains any of the above signals but the user has not asked for a HITL, flag it:
151	
152	> "This process includes [signal]. Before the automation [action], a human should review [data]. I recommend inserting a HITL node here — want me to add it?"
153	
154	Then proceed to Step 3 (schema design) only after the user confirms.

1	# Public Safety
2	
3	This skill is intended for a public skills repository. Keep all content, examples, fixtures, logs, and commits safe to publish.
4	
5	## Never include
6	
7	- Raw exported BPMN from customers, tenants, demos, or operator-supplied examples.
8	- Tenant URLs, organization names, folder keys, connection IDs, release keys, queue IDs, process IDs, user IDs, or email addresses.
9	- Private process names, business payloads, screenshots, exported package contents, or traces.
10	- Local absolute paths from developer machines.
11	- Temporary mission notes, task transcripts, or Rookery-only context.
12	- Internal-only repository paths as runtime instructions for the skill user.
13	
14	## Use instead
15	
16	- Synthetic process names such as `InvoiceApproval`.
17	- Synthetic element IDs such as `Task_ValidateRequest`.
18	- Placeholder resource labels such as `<PROCESS_NAME>`, `<FOLDER_KEY>`, or `<CONNECTION_NAME>` when the user must provide a real value.
19	- Short structural examples that demonstrate XML shape without private data.
20	- Summaries of behavior rather than copied private XML.
21	
22	## XML placeholder escaping
23	
24	Angle-bracket placeholders are safe only when the XML location can contain text
25	or CDATA. In XML attributes, escape the brackets so the BPMN remains
26	well-formed:
27	
28	- Attribute values: `value="<TENANT_URL>"`,
29	  `value="<FOLDER_KEY>"`, `value="<CONNECTION_NAME>"`.
30	- Element text or CDATA: `<TENANT_URL>`, `<FOLDER_KEY>`, and
31	  `<CONNECTION_NAME>` may be used as literal placeholder text.
32	
33	After sanitizing a BPMN file, parse it before reporting done. A sanitization
34	pass that replaces a private value with unescaped `<PLACEHOLDER>` inside an
35	attribute has made the file invalid.
36	
37	## Review checklist
38	
39	Before committing:
40	
41	- Search changed files for local path fragments, URLs, IDs, and private names.
42	- Confirm every example can be understood without access to internal repositories.
43	- Confirm Integration Service examples do not contain real connector resource identifiers.
44	- Confirm generated package metadata examples are synthetic or omitted.
45

1	# Expression Authoring
2	
3	Use this reference whenever pass 2 writes Maestro runtime expressions in BPMN
4	XML. Pass 1 may use business-readable placeholder conditions; pass 2 replaces
5	them with expressions only after the variables and scopes exist.
6	
7	## Stored expression shape
8	
9	- Use a leading `=` where Maestro expects expression content.
10	- Treat values without `=` as literals.
11	- Read BPMN variables through `vars.<variableId>`, for example
12	  `=vars.Var_RequestId`.
13	- Do not use bare variable names such as `=requestId` in generated runtime XML.
14	- Context bindings use `=bindings.<bindingId>`.
15	- Current element outputs use `result` only in output mappings for that
16	  element. For new BPMN script tasks, return an object and expose its value
17	  through `result.response`: use `return { response: value };` with
18	  `source="=result.response"` for a scalar variable, or return a nested object
19	  and use `source="=result.response.<field>"` for a field. Do not use
20	  `source="=result"` with a bare scalar return in live debug/runtime BPMN; the
21	  run can complete while the mapped variable reads back empty.
22	- Multi-instance task bodies read the current item from `iterator.item`.
23	- Multi-instance subprocess bodies read the current item from
24	  `iterator[0].item`. Use `iterator[1].item` (and so on) inside nested
25	  multi-instance subprocesses: the index counts nesting depth from outermost
26	  (`[0]`) to innermost.
27	- The current 0-based loop index inside any multi-instance body is exposed as
28	  `iterator.loopCounter` for tasks and `iterator[N].loopCounter` for
29	  subprocesses at depth N.
30	- Error mapping conditions may inspect the built-in error object through
31	  `vars.error`, for example `=vars.error.code == "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE"`.
32	
33	## Inline JavaScript with `=js:`
34	
35	When a mapping body or context value needs computation that a simple
36	`=vars.<id>` expression cannot express, prefix the body with `=js:` and follow
37	it with a JavaScript expression. The runtime evaluates the rest of the value
38	against the same `vars`, `bindings`, `result`, and `iterator` namespaces.
39	Use this form inside CDATA mapping bodies; it is the runtime-supported
40	escape hatch the BPMN expression grammar does not otherwise expose.
41	
42	```xml
43	<uipath:input name="JobArguments" type="json" target="bodyField"><![CDATA[
44	{"startRow":"=js:iterator[0].loopCounter * vars.Var_RowsPerShard",
45	 "endRow":"=js:(iterator[0].loopCounter + 1) * vars.Var_RowsPerShard - 1"}
46	]]></uipath:input>
47	```
48	
49	Rules:
50	
51	- The prefix is `=js:` (case-sensitive, no space).
52	- The body must still satisfy lint-sensitive constraints: no assignment
53	  operators in fields where read-only expressions are required.
54	- Prefer plain `=vars.<id>` or `=bindings.<id>` when the value does not need
55	  computation — `=js:` should be reserved for arithmetic, string
56	  manipulation, or conditional selection.
57	- A `=js:` expression that returns an object or array must produce valid JSON
58	  for fields typed `json`.
59	
60	Prefer JavaScript-safe variable ids such as `Var_RequestId`. If a brownfield
61	file contains non-identifier ids, preserve them and let the product editor or
62	CLI normalize the access form; do not silently rename variables without updating
63	all mappings, expressions, and generated metadata.
64	
65	## Lint-sensitive fields
66	
67	These fields must be read-only expressions:
68	
69	- Gateway `bpmn:conditionExpression` values.
70	- Activity skip conditions.
71	- Multi-instance completion and filter conditions.
72	- `uipath:errorMapping` condition values.
73	- Mapping values that read variables or element outputs.
74	
75	Do not use assignment operators in these fields. Comparisons such as `==`,
76	`===`, `!=`, `!==`, `>=`, and `<=` are allowed.
77	
78	## Scope and availability
79	
80	- Root variables are visible across the root process after they are declared and
81	  reachable by control flow.
82	- An output variable you intend to expose in runtime inspection (via
83	  `debug-instance variables-all` or `instance variables`) must be root-scoped —
84	  declare its `uipath:output` or `uipath:inputOutput` WITHOUT an `elementId`. A
85	  variable scoped with `elementId` is bound to that element and is not surfaced
86	  as a root/global runtime variable. Preserve exact variable ids: if the
87	  requested variable id is `product`, declare `id="product"` and map to
88	  `var="product"`, not `Product` or `Var_Product`. Current BPMN live debug may
89	  expose the root output definition while still returning the value as `null`;
90	  treat that as a runtime/debug API limitation, not proof that the authored
91	  mapping is absent.
92	- Subprocess variables stay scoped to that subprocess.
93	- Output mappings should target `uipath:inputOutput` or `uipath:output`
94	  variables, not read-only `uipath:input` variables.
95	- Entry point inputs that must later be updated need a separate mutable
96	  `uipath:inputOutput` variable and an explicit mapping from the entry input.
97	- Trigger-bound values are commonly represented as `uipath:inputOutput`
98	  variables scoped with `elementId` so the trigger can write them during
99	  execution.
100	
101	## Common mistakes
102	
103	- `=requestId` instead of `=vars.Var_RequestId`.
104	- `var="requestId"` instead of `var="Var_RequestId"`.
105	- Using `result` outside the output mapping of the element that produced it.
106	- Reading `iterator[0].item` outside the multi-instance subprocess body.
107	- Moving a variable into a subprocess without updating mappings that read it
108	  from the root scope.
109
